project.name: file
project.commit_note: The staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/file` is used for line mapping and matches the saved MSan frames at `mcopy:1225`, `mget:1365/1602`, `match:296`, `file_softmagic:108`, `file_buffer:254`, and `magic_buffer:547`.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an out-of-range regex search over bytes beyond the logical 6-byte input. A truncated sfnt header routes libmagic through `magic/Magdir/fonts` into `sfnt-font`; `mcopy(FILE_REGEX)` then uses `offset=12` against `nbytes=6`, derives a 320-byte search window starting past the witness, and `memchr` reads unrelated uninitialized heap bytes.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42483783 (file): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target magic_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42483783
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / magic/Magdir/fonts
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 6-byte file `00 01 00 00 00 20`. In libmagic's soft-magic engine, those bytes match `magic/Magdir/fonts:153` (`0 string \000\001\000\000`) and then take the `>0 use sfnt-font` continuation at line 154. Inside the named `sfnt-font` block, the `>4 ubeshort <47` rule at line 163 accepts the witness's `numTables` field `0x0020 = 32`, so execution reaches the next continuation `>>12 regex/4l \^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z][A-Za-z/][A-Za-z2\ ]` at line 167. That rule enters `mcopy()` with `type = FILE_REGEX`, `offset = 12`, and `nbytes = 6`. Vulnerable `mcopy(FILE_REGEX)` checks only `s == NULL`, not `nbytes < offset`, so the `regex/4l` flags derive `linecnt = 4` and `bytecnt = 320`, and the later clamp against `nbytes - offset` fails because `6 - 12` underflows in `size_t`. `buf` therefore becomes `s + 12` and `end` becomes `s + 332`, so the newline-scanning `memchr` loop at `src/softmagic.c:1225` scans 320 bytes starting six bytes past the end of the witness. MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in that `memchr` call. The fix adds the missing `|| nbytes < offset` precondition before any FILE_REGEX window arithmetic.

source.description: First project read on the observed path. In the top-level fonts rule `magic/Magdir/fonts:153`, `mcopy` materializes the exact 6-byte witness into `ms->ms_value` so libmagic can compare the sfnt signature and route into the `sfnt-font` named rule.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is exactly 6 bytes `00 01 00 00 00 20` (sha256 `759910ebafe001a6f0068655fdf6ca4565650f6da9c77047468f138cb7ce89bf`). These bytes are a truncated sfnt header: version `0x00010000`, followed by `numTables = 0x0020`.

sink.code:
for (lines = linecnt, b = buf; lines && b < end &&
     ((b = CAST(const char *,
         memchr(c = b, '\n', CAST(size_t, (end - b)))))
     || (b = CAST(const char *,

sink.description: MSan crash site. The FILE_REGEX newline scan runs `memchr` over the out-of-range search window `[s + 12, s + 332)`, so it reads uninitialized bytes from unrelated heap memory instead of from the 6-byte witness.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memchr at offset 5 inside [0x70100000006c, 320)` and attributes the poisoned bytes to a prior heap allocation reached after the regex window escaped the logical input.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The FILE_REGEX precondition rejects only a NULL source pointer; it does not reject `nbytes < offset`. That lets the `sfnt-font` regex continuation run with `offset = 12` on a 6-byte buffer.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this condition to `if (s == NULL || nbytes < offset)`, which is exactly the missing obligation on the reproduced path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-driving state is the exact truncated sfnt header and total length `nbytes = 6`. Those values make the top-level fonts rule match, make `numTables = 32` pass the `sfnt-font` guard, and leave no valid bytes at the later regex offset 12.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact staged witness is the 6-byte file `00 01 00 00 00 20`, which the fuzzer passes directly into libmagic as `data,size`.

Source. In the top-level fonts rule `magic/Magdir/fonts:153` (`0 string \000\001\000\000`), this invocation copies the 6-byte witness from `s + 0` into `ms->ms_value`. That materializes the attacker-controlled sfnt header bytes that steer the later named-rule path.

For the same fonts rule, `file_strncmp` compares the copied bytes against the literal `\000\001\000\000`. The first four witness bytes match, so this top-level rule succeeds and `match()` reaches the continuation `>0 use sfnt-font` at `magic/Magdir/fonts:154`.
The matched continuation `>0 use sfnt-font` resolves the named `sfnt-font` rule set and recursively matches it against the same witness buffer with base `offset + o = 0`.

Inside `sfnt-font`, `match()` advances to continuation `magic/Magdir/fonts:163` (`>4 ubeshort <47`) and stores that rule's relative offset `4` in `ms->offset`. With no `OFFADD`, this continuation will read byte 4 of the same 6-byte witness.

depends_on.via: rv = match(ms, ml.magic, ml.nmagic, s, nbytes, offset + o, mode, text, flip, indir_count, name_count, printed_something, need_separator, returnval);

fine_trace.note: For that `ubeshort` continuation, `mcopy` uses `offset = 4` and the 6-byte total length to reduce the copy to the two remaining bytes, then copies witness bytes `00 20` into `ms->ms_value`.
The `FILE_BESHORT` conversion interprets the copied bytes as a big-endian 16-bit value. From `00 20`, it produces `p->h = 32`.

For `magic/Magdir/fonts:163`, `magiccheck` uses `v = p->h = 32` for `FILE_BESHORT` and applies the rule's unsigned relation `<47`. The comparison succeeds, so the `sfnt-font` chain continues past this guard.

Because step 7 matched, `match()` advances to continuation `magic/Magdir/fonts:167` (`>>12 regex/4l ...`) and stores that rule's relative offset `12` in `ms->offset`. This is the source-level origin of the later regex offset.

fine_trace.code:
if (mcopy(ms, p, m->type, m->flag & INDIR, s, (uint32_t)(offset + o),
    (uint32_t)nbytes, m) == -1)
fine_trace.note: For the regex continuation, `mget` combines `ms->offset = 12` from step 8 with the named-rule base `o = 0` and calls `mcopy` with `type = FILE_REGEX`, `offset = 12`, and `nbytes = 6`.

Root cause. In the FILE_REGEX arm, the only early rejection is `s == NULL`. The reproduced call has `s != NULL` but `nbytes = 6 < offset = 12`, and vulnerable code does not reject that precondition before using `offset`. The patch adds `|| nbytes < offset` here.

The `regex/4l` flags set `m->str_range = 4` and line-count mode, so `linecnt = 4` and `bytecnt = 320`. Because step 10 let `offset = 12` survive against `nbytes = 6`, the unsigned expression `nbytes - offset` underflows and the clamp does not shrink `bytecnt`.

fine_trace.code:
buf = RCAST(const char *, s) + offset;
end = last = RCAST(const char *, s) + bytecnt + offset;
fine_trace.note: With `offset = 12` and `bytecnt = 320`, FILE_REGEX defines the search window `[s + 12, s + 332)`. It starts six bytes past the end of the 6-byte witness and spans unrelated heap memory.

fine_trace.code:
for (lines = linecnt, b = buf; lines && b < end &&
     ((b = CAST(const char *,
	 memchr(c = b, '\n', CAST(size_t, (end - b)))))
     || (b = CAST(const char *,
	 memchr(c, '\r', CAST(size_t, (end - c))))));
fine_trace.note: Sink. `memchr` scans the out-of-range 320-byte window from step 12. The saved MSan trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memchr at offset 5 inside [0x70100000006c, 320)` at this loop.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The fix adds the missing `nbytes < offset` rejection in `mcopy(FILE_REGEX)`, which is exactly the violated precondition on the reproduced `sfnt-font` regex path.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: No — MSAN's origin stack identifies the unrelated heap allocation whose uninitialized bytes were reached after the regex window escaped the 6-byte witness. The project bug is the missing `nbytes < offset` guard in `mcopy(FILE_REGEX)`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `/bin/arvo run` in the prepared ARVO workspace container, which executed `magic_fuzzer` on `poc` and wrote `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `reproduction_report.json` reporting `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `mcopy`.

format.name: Exact 6-byte truncated sfnt header witness
format.contract: The available evidence proves the exact staged witness only: the 6-byte file `00 01 00 00 00 20`. Its first four bytes must match the sfnt signature rule `magic/Magdir/fonts:153`, its `numTables` field must be `0x0020` so `magic/Magdir/fonts:163` (`>4 ubeshort <47`) succeeds, and the total file length must still be only 6 bytes so the later `magic/Magdir/fonts:167` regex continuation executes with `offset = 12 > nbytes = 6`. The staged artifacts do not establish a broader class beyond this exact witness and this specific `sfnt-font` rule chain.
